newsitem.title: CHINA: China city cuts higher cost of being foreigner.
newsitem.headline: China city cuts higher cost of being foreigner.

text.p: In China's southern boomtown of Shenzhen, the days when your face determines the price you are charged are numbered.

The local government has announced that from January 1 next year it will start to treat foreigners like Chinese citizens by allowing foreigners to pay local rates instead of "foreigner prices", Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
All foreigners in the city, from businessmen to back-packers, would pay local rates for accommodation, medical bills and tourist sites, instead of higher "foreigner prices", it said.
It did not say whether other fees would be standardised.
Officials contacted in Shenzhen, which borders Hong Kong, had no additional information on the move.
Last month, the government of the southern province of Guangdong said it would ease curbs on the sale and marketing in China of products by foreign-invested companies.
That move was seen as aimed at equalising treatment of foreign companies to meet requirements for China's plans to join the World Trade Organisation.

Shenzhen is the first city in China to take steps to phase out the widespread practice of setting special prices for foreigners who must pay extra for everything from rail and air tickets to hotels and tourist sites.
A ticket to the popular Forbidden City in Beijing costs 85 yuan ($10.20) for foreigners and 20 yuan ($2.40) for Chinese citizens.
